title: No More Screens for Little Kids in LA Schools!
summary: Imagine walking into your classroom on the first day of school and hearing your teacher say, "Put away your laptops—we're not using screens today!" That's exactly what's happening in Los Angeles, the second-biggest school district in the country. Starting this week, kids in 1st grade and under get no screen time at all. Later this year, older elementary, middle, and high schoolers will have limits too. That's over 400,000 students! Why the big change? The school board wants kids to spend less time staring at screens. Last year, they already banned cell phones. A teacher named Kirti Baranwal did a lesson on screen addiction. She asked her students to check their own screen time. Many came back with 8 or 10 hours a day—even without phones in school! "I was like, when are you sleeping?" she said. But not everyone is happy. Science teacher Armaghan Khan uses laptops for cool experiments, like a car crash simulator to learn about forces. He says he wasn't given much help to switch to no screens. "I don't feel like I'm being set up for success," he told NPR. The district says this year is a test. They'll put software on devices to track screen time, but it won't shut them off. At the end of the year, they'll look at the data to see what worked. Some things, like digital textbooks, are still okay. But teachers have lots of questions. For now, everyone is trying to figure out: if kids aren't on screens, what should they be doing instead?
why_it_matters: This story shows how adults are trying to help kids balance screen time, which can affect how you learn and play at school.

background_read: Many schools across the US are trying to reduce screen time for young children, because too much screen use can affect sleep and learning.
Los Angeles (a big city in California) has the second-largest school district in the country.
NPR (short for National Public Radio, a news organization that tells stories about what's happening around the country) spoke to teachers about the change.
Article_Structure: WHO: The Los Angeles school district, its students, and teachers like Kirti Baranwal and Armaghan Khan
WHAT: The school district is banning all screens for young kids and setting limits for older students
WHERE: In Los Angeles, the second-biggest school district in the United States
WHY: Because the school board wants to reduce screen time after seeing how many hours kids spend on screens, even without phones in school

perspectives.description: Teachers like Kirti Baranwal think less screen time will help kids learn better and get more sleep, because many students were shocked by their own high screen use.
Science teacher Armaghan Khan uses screens for hands-on experiments, like a car crash simulator, and feels the district didn't give him enough help to switch to no-screen lessons.
They see this year as a test and will collect data on screen time to decide what works best, without shutting devices off completely.
